The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of RNN-based CL methods is not directly determined by the sequence length, but rather by the working memory requirements, i.e., the amount of information that must be kept in memory to process a given task.
RNNs require additional considerations when learning sequential data.
CL in RNN is not fundamentally more difficult than in feedforward networks, but requires careful considerations to ensure that the working memory requirements are not too high.
